source_row.rationale: NIOSH recommends local exhaust control because surgical smoke can contain hazardous gases, vapors, particles, bioaerosols, and cellular material. Option C states the infection/occupational-safety purpose. The other choices are not the function of surgical-smoke evacuation.
source_row.source_detail: NIOSH Hazard Controls HC11: surgical smoke can contain toxic gases, vapors, bioaerosols and cellular material; local exhaust ventilation/smoke evacuation should capture smoke close to its source and remain active whenever airborne particles are produced. DHHS (NIOSH) Publication 96-128; page last reviewed 2014 and recommendation remains referenced by current NIOSH surgical-smoke guidance; live currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
